votes.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendments — An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes (H R 5334)
votes.plain_language: The House voted to accept the Senate's rewrite of H.R. 5334, which imposes Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, extends an Iran sanctions law, and also expands a teacher tax deduction to early-childhood educators. A Yea accepts that Senate version. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 93)
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress authorizes it, except for forces needed to defend against an imminent attack if the President follows the War Powers Resolution's time limits. A Yea agrees. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Whistleblower Protection Act (H R 4646)
votes.plain_language: This bill extends whistleblower protections to employees of Housing and Urban Development contractors and grantees, including on contracts signed before 2013. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Table — Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors (H RES 1486)
votes.plain_language: The resolution would impeach President Trump over Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection practices that it says violate the Constitution. This vote was a motion to table, which kills the resolution. A Yea tables it; a Nay would have left it pending.

lobbying.bill_title: Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act (H R 3276)

lobbying.bill_title: Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act

votes.question: On Passage — To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective (H R 9436)
votes.plain_language: This bill moves the deadline for new lobster- and crab-gear rules meant to protect North Atlantic right whales from 2028 to 2035. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

lobbying.bill_title: To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective (H R 9436)
votes.plain_language: H.R. 9436 would move the deadline for new lobster- and crab-gear rules meant to protect North Atlantic right whales from 2028 to 2035. votes.plain_language: This bill provides FY2027 appropriations for military construction, the Department of Veterans Affairs, and related agencies. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8469)
votes.bill_title: Making appropriations for military construction, the Department of Veterans Affairs, and related agencies for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, and for other purposes.
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8469 is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to redirect $481,832,000 from the NATO Security Investment Program account to the Military Construction, Defense-Wide account.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Setting forth the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2026 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2027 through 2035 (S CON RES 33)
votes.bill_title: A concurrent resolution setting forth the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2026 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2027 through 2035.
votes.plain_language: This concurrent resolution establishes the congressional budget for the federal government for FY2026, sets forth budgetary levels for FY2027-FY2035, and provides reconciliation instructions for legislation that increases the deficit. A Yea agrees to the concurrent resolution; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Pay Our Homeland Defenders Act (H R 8029)
votes.bill_title: Pay Our Homeland Defenders Act
votes.plain_language: This bill provides appropriations to the Department of Homeland Security for the remainder of FY2026. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Pay Our Homeland Defenders Act (H R 8029)
votes.bill_title: Pay Our Homeland Defenders Act
votes.plain_language: H.R. 8029 (Pay Our Homeland Defenders Act) provides appropriations to the Department of Homeland Security for the remainder of FY2026. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States requiring a balanced budget for the Federal Government (H J RES 139)
votes.bill_title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States requiring a balanced budget for the Federal Government.
votes.plain_language: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment prohibiting total federal expenditures for a year from exceeding the average annual federal receipts collected in the three prior years, adjusted for changes in the population of U.S. citizens and inflation. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 7744)
votes.bill_title: Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill provides appropriations to the Department of Homeland Security for the remainder of FY2026. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 7744)
votes.bill_title: Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: H.R. 7744 (Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026) provides appropriations to the Department of Homeland Security for the remainder of FY2026. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendments — Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 7148)
votes.bill_title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill provides appropriations to several federal departments and agencies for the remainder of FY2026, provides continuing FY2026 appropriations for the Department of Homeland Security through February 13, 2026, and extends various expiring programs. This vote was on accepting the Senate's changes, which sends the bill to the President. A Yea accepts the Senate version; a Nay rejects it.

votes.question: On Passage — Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 7148)
votes.bill_title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill provides appropriations to several federal departments and agencies for the remainder of FY2026 and provides continuing FY2026 appropriations for the Department of Homeland Security through February 13, 2026. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7148)
votes.bill_title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7148 (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to prohibit the use of funds for certain community funding projects.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7148)
votes.bill_title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7148 (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to prohibit the use of funds to implement section 24220 of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, including any requirements enabling or supporting vehicle "kill switch" technology, and to prohibit federal spending for the execution or enforcement of such authorities.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Making further consolidated appropriations for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026, and for other purposes (H R 7147)
votes.bill_title: Homeland Security and Further Additional Continuing Appropriations Act, 2026.
votes.plain_language: This bill provides continuing FY2026 appropriations to the Department of Homeland Security through May 22, 2026. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 7006)
votes.bill_title: Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill provides FY2026 appropriations to several federal departments and agencies for activities and programs related to financial services, general government, national security, the administration of foreign affairs, and foreign assistance. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7006)
votes.bill_title: Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7006 is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to eliminate funding for the National Endowment for Democracy.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7006)
votes.bill_title: Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7006 is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to reduce the District of Columbia District and Appeals Court funding by 20% and to strike the salary and expense funding for Judges Boasberg's and Judge Boardman's staffs.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — AGOA Extension Act (H R 6500)
votes.bill_title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
votes.plain_language: This bill provides continuing FY2027 appropriations for federal agencies and extends various expiring programs and authorities. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 6938)
votes.bill_title: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill provides FY2026 appropriations to several federal departments and agencies for activities and programs related to commerce, law enforcement, science, energy and water development, public lands, and the environment. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Retaining Divisions B and C — Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 6938)
votes.bill_title: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: H.R. 6938 combines three FY2026 spending bills: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment. The House voted separately on whether to keep parts of the bill. This vote was on keeping Divisions B and C. A Yea keeps them in the bill; a Nay would remove them.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
